routing_warnings.description: The decision to show digital-platform, program-management, and contingency or reserve costs as separate total-program-capex line items belongs to the independently defined program-wide capex Requirement.
The minimum DSCR and equity-IRR thresholds govern availability-payment sizing rather than the independent production of the debt schedule and coverage output.
The reported failure is that the dashboards do not clearly present debt performance; it does not establish failure of the underlying debt schedule or DSCR calculation.
The observed failure to display project returns clearly is specifically a dashboard-presentation failure and should not be duplicated as a runtime failure for return calculation.
This message requires evidence that user fees alone are insufficient and belongs to the availability-payment necessity Requirement rather than the payment-sizing mechanism.
The claim about separate cash flows for both funding scenarios supports the scenario-comparison Requirement but does not establish implementation of the DSCR-and-equity-IRR payment-sizing rule.
This message establishes the required conclusion that user fees alone are insufficient and an availability payment is necessary; it does not independently change the Case F versus Case G comparison.
The client's inability to understand the presentation and follow how figures were generated primarily concerns model comprehensibility.
The clause about dashboards failing to show returns, debt performance, and bankability concerns the dashboard Requirement.
The claim that every number traces to a source on the Assumptions tab concerns assumption disclosure and traceability rather than calculation integrity.
The freelancer's claim about providing a simplified dashboard is implementation evidence for the dashboard Requirement, not a target-specific calculation-integrity claim.
The request for a professional, clear, and strongly presented finished model primarily specifies government-submission presentation quality rather than model navigation or comprehensibility.
This message reports delivery of the Excel working file but does not claim that the model's usability or comprehensibility requirement was satisfied.
The complaint that the model is unclear and its figures cannot be followed primarily concerns overall model comprehensibility rather than the dashboard specifically.
The reported difficulty understanding the delivered material is not dashboard-specific and is better routed to the model-usability Requirement.
The request for flawless modeling primarily concerns calculation and modeling quality rather than presentation formatting.
The message specifically requires robust evidence that user fees alone cannot make the project viable or bankable.
The client's report that the spreadsheet has many issues and is unusable concerns model quality or correctness, not whether the deliverable was provided in Excel format.
The client's report that the delivered material is difficult to understand concerns model usability and quality rather than the Excel file-format Requirement.
